# Practical Guides

> Free public resources for finding official service routes, examining manipulative language, and judging alarming information. Each project records its own scope, sources and limits. This index helps readers and tools find the published material; it does not certify impartiality or verification.

## Collection and methods

- [Collection homepage](https://extivaries.github.io/How-to-Hear-a-Bully/practical-guides/): choose a resource by the question you need to answer.
- [How we check our work](https://extivaries.github.io/How-to-Hear-a-Bully/practical-guides/methods.html): scope, evidence, review dates, AI assistance, correction routes and project-specific reuse terms.
- [Methods in Markdown](https://extivaries.github.io/How-to-Hear-a-Bully/docs/practical-guides/methods.md)
- [Sitemap](https://extivaries.github.io/How-to-Hear-a-Bully/sitemap.xml): the six HTML pages hosted in this project. Middleman has its own hosting and sitemap.

## Don't Pay a Middleman

- [Directory](https://dont-pay-a-middleman.vercel.app/): official U.S. federal self-service routes and fees. Government fees and payments to a helper are different; paid expertise, translation or representation may be valuable.
- [Methods and verification](https://dont-pay-a-middleman.vercel.app/about#verification): source checks and their limits. Check current requirements and fees with the official agency before acting.
- [Corrections and contact](https://dont-pay-a-middleman.vercel.app/about#contact): this project has its own contact route and privacy/response limits.

## How to Hear a Bully

- [Guide](https://extivaries.github.io/How-to-Hear-a-Bully/): a civic-literacy guide to manipulative political accusations and labels. It distinguishes disagreement, unsupported claims, misleading impressions, corrections, and intimidation or misuse of power; "not enough evidence to know" remains a valid conclusion. About 3,800 words.
- [Source notes and verification](https://extivaries.github.io/How-to-Hear-a-Bully/notes.html): historical texts, political case records, psychological research, U.S. defamation law, contrary evidence and remaining uncertainties.
- [Guide in Markdown](https://extivaries.github.io/How-to-Hear-a-Bully/how-to-hear-a-bully.md)
- [Notes in Markdown](https://extivaries.github.io/How-to-Hear-a-Bully/how-to-hear-a-bully-notes.md)
- [Revision ledger](https://extivaries.github.io/How-to-Hear-a-Bully/notes.html#revision-ledger)

Citation: Exti. How to Hear a Bully: Recognizing the Language of Power and Manipulation. Second edition, October 2026. The edition date does not establish when every source was last checked. Historical context includes Thucydides, Confucius, Tacitus, seditious libel and Orwell; political examples include McCarthy, Reid, Trump, Biden and Putin. Apply the same questions to favored and disfavored speakers.

## Why Does Everything Feel Like a Crisis?

- [Guide](https://extivaries.github.io/How-to-Hear-a-Bully/crisis/): judging alarming information and choosing a response, with five questions and two fictional flood exercises. About 1,900 words. The questions can support greater concern as well as reassurance; current emergency instructions take priority.
- [Nine source notes](https://extivaries.github.io/How-to-Hear-a-Bully/crisis/notes.html): study designs, findings, uncertainties and access limits. Clicks, bodily responses, mood, stress symptoms, opinions and actual danger are different outcomes.
- [Guide in Markdown](https://extivaries.github.io/How-to-Hear-a-Bully/docs/crisis-guide/why-does-everything-feel-like-a-crisis.md)
- [Notes in Markdown](https://extivaries.github.io/How-to-Hear-a-Bully/docs/crisis-guide/why-does-everything-feel-like-a-crisis-notes.md)

Editorial review: 9 October 2026. First web publication: 9 October 2026. The teaching method has not been tested with readers; it is not a clinical treatment or a validated danger score. Canonical citation links are the guide and source-note URLs above; section and numbered-note anchors provide more precise references.

## Related tool: Climate and growing

- [Plant Climate Map](https://plantclimatemap.org/): explore Köppen–Geiger climate classifications and USDA plant hardiness zones across the 48 contiguous United States. A separate app with its own map information and data sources; the guides' editorial review dates and reuse terms do not cover the map or its data.

## Corrections and reuse

- [Report a correction for Bully, Crisis or the collection](https://github.com/ExtiVaries/How-to-Hear-a-Bully/issues): public GitHub issues, requiring a GitHub account.
- [Reuse terms](https://extivaries.github.io/How-to-Hear-a-Bully/practical-guides/methods.html#reading-and-reuse): Bully and its notes use CC BY 4.0 plus an author permission for noncommercial use without credit. Commercial use requires the specified credit and link; third-party quotations are excluded. This license does not extend to the other projects. Reuse terms for Crisis and collection material remain undecided.

This optional link index is not required for search indexing or AI citation and cannot guarantee either. The linked source notes, not this index, provide the evidence for the guides' factual claims. Research dates are not automatically renewed when metadata or links change.
